description: The one identifier grammar of the Workbench: every identifier kind (pattern, normaliser, alias kinds, carrying fields per system with the upstream code that writes them), the mention patterns used to find identifiers in text, technical identifier grammars of live sources, and the cross-system keys declared as link bindings. ontology/identifiers.py loads and compiles this file.

tiers.verified: A key the owning system writes and resolves on; may still be non-unique (then a candidate, never a merge).
tiers.lead: A reference only: it finds candidates and never asserts identity.

identity_rules.auto_merge: No PurchaseOrder, SalesOrder, AssemblyOrder or invoice ever auto-merges on a normalised value.
identity_rules.exact: An exact match is the literal comparison the owning system makes (Portal TRIM/ILIKE).
identity_rules.normalised: A normalised value or blocking key only finds candidates.
identity_rules.exact_compare: Per kind, the literal comparison that makes a match exact (a case root), read by plx.find and find_root through ontology/identifiers.exact_compare: trim = equal after trimming both sides, case-sensitive (Portal resolveOrderByNumber: order_number = TRIM($1), plx-customer-portal@59b0548 portal/src/lib/orders/order-identity.ts:92-99); trim_casefold = equal after trimming, case-insensitive, with no wildcard (Portal TRIM(po_number) ILIKE TRIM($1), portal/src/app/api/mrp/receiving/open-po-lines/route.ts:279; a % or _ in the value is literal); normalized = equal after the kind's own normaliser on both sides (Portal customer PO: normalizePoReference, trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed, upper case, plx-customer-portal@40f7802 portal/src/lib/orders/customer-po.ts:17-24).
identity_rules.carrier_roles: primary: the field the owning system resolves the identifier on; alias: a field holding the same record's number in another system or column (its record is the primary's twin, operating/ontology_tools_investigate._root_twins); linked_alias: an alias whose record is the primary's twin only when a verified same-record link joins them, because its writer renames on a clash (a same-number match alone names another record); separate_row: another record holding the same number; lead: a reference that finds candidates only; mention: free text.
identity_rules.identity_scope: A kind that declares identity_scope is unique only within it: its identity is (scope space, scope value, normalised value), read through ontology/identifiers.identity_key with the carrier's scope_field from the same record (identity_scope). Two values of two scopes are two identities; a value whose record holds no scope value names no identity. A query names no scope, so plx.find and find_root (operating/ontology_tools.exact_match, identity_scopes) make such a value exact only on a record holding a scope value whose scope space holds the value under that one scope, and then by its literal trimmed text, not exact_compare: any other match is a lead. A carrier may qualify its scope with scope_within (company: the record's BC company, as BC numbers repeat across companies) and name records that never hold the value with scope_excludes (field and values: the Portal skips a cancelled order); an excluded record is a lead and never makes the value ambiguous.

environment_prefixes.meaning: The Portal's environment reference prefix (NEXT_PUBLIC_UAT_REF_PREFIX): numbers a Portal database issues while the variable is set start with it. The Portal's own series checks strip it (isCanonicalSalesOrderNumber, isCanonicalShipmentNumber, isLegacyFmPoNumber) but every join compares the literal value. A value carrying it was issued by a prefix-setting Portal database; the staging app that drains Business Central writes plx-postgres-uat, while the reporting API serves the replica of plx-postgres-staging, so such a number may name a row the reporting API never serves. A diagnosis only: never stripped for a match. The one list of prefixes: a kind marked environment_prefixed accepts its value_pattern behind any of them (ontology/identifiers.py compiles the prefix into the grammar), so no value_pattern writes a prefix itself; petra_po keeps its own parser for the UAT- part of a Petra PO.

amazon_seller_sku.description: An Amazon seller SKU usable as an SP-API query value (single inner spaces, at most 40 characters). Not a PLX item code: equal-looking codes are no match (FBA-05).

freightcom_id.description: Freightcom Customer API shipment (booking) id, one path segment.

mail_labelled.description: Label-backed identifier claims in mail/document text for Graph evidence; the delimiter after the label is optional (callers then require a digit).

patterns.upstream: the receipt_lab_id grammar behind a receipt / receipt lab id / lab id label (a bare "lab" stays the RP shape): the raw YYDDD-N form has no self-delimiting shape, so prose ("linked to receipt 26161-1") reads it only by its label
a Business Central document No. (Code[20], the bc_document_no grammar) behind a Business Central / BC document label; the free Code[20] has no shape of its own

document_labelled.description: Label-backed identifier claims in extracted document text (a ':' or '#' delimiter is required; the value ends at whitespace or a separator).

ao_form.description: Short shop-floor AO form labels; mapping them to Product / SalesOrder is an interpretation (review-grade).

document_item_line.description: A labelled item code that heads a line-item block.

document_title_ao.description: An AO code in a file name or title: an identity lead, never source-asserted.

petra_po_attached.description: Petra PO numbers written with their prefix (po-number-series.ts / create-fm-purchase-order.ts shapes).

petra_po_labelled.description: A PO number separated from its label ('PO 4821', 'P.O. # 4821', 'Our PO 4821', 'Purchase Order No. 106089'); the value is the number as written.

supplier_reference.description: A supplier's own labelled number (order / confirmation / proforma / invoice / reference); group 1 is the label, group 2 the value.

pi_attached.description: A proforma-invoice reference written as one token (PI-ABC001234, PI40404).

shapes.description: Self-delimiting identifier shapes the scanner finds without a label.

link_bindings.name: fm_order_entry_to_sales_order
link_bindings.note: FM OE <-> gold SO bridge; written by ensure-sales-order-from-fm-oe. Hollow-stub order numbers are not filtered on this path.

link_bindings.name: sage_order_to_sales_order
link_bindings.note: Sage ETL upserts gold SOs keyed by sageOrdUniq.

link_bindings.name: portal_entity_to_bc_number
link_bindings.note: app_bc_entity_map.bc_number (status LINKED) is the identity link; the map is not served by the reporting API.

link_bindings.name: portal_entity_to_bc_system_id
link_bindings.note: bc_system_id; not served.

link_bindings.name: sales_order_po_reference_to_bc_sales_order
link_bindings.note: externalDocumentNumber = po_reference (truncated to 35). po_reference is not unique and can hold a name. The PO is unique only per customer: a lead across two customers is never one identity (identity_scope).

link_bindings.name: sales_order_number_to_bc_sales_invoice
link_bindings.note: Invoice externalDocumentNumber = order_number at posting; order_number is rewritten to the BC No. after drain.

link_bindings.name: gold_po_to_fm_po
link_bindings.note: The FM PO with a gold twin is the gold PO; its ponumber is an alias of the gold row.

link_bindings.name: gold_po_fm_number
link_bindings.note: Number fallback when fmGeneratedPoId is absent.

link_bindings.name: gold_po_renumbered_to_bc
link_bindings.note: Written together with po_number = BC No.; fmPoNumber keeps the earlier number.

link_bindings.name: bc_po_your_reference
link_bindings.note: Your Reference is not in BC API v2.0 purchaseOrders.

link_bindings.name: sales_order_renumbered_to_bc
link_bindings.note: fmOeNumber keeps the earlier order number.

link_bindings.name: product_to_bc_item
link_bindings.note: BC Item No. = code truncated to 20, compared case-insensitively.

link_bindings.name: product_to_sage_item
link_bindings.note: Cutover match key, not the BC No.

link_bindings.name: product_to_fm_record
link_bindings.note: external_id is not unique on app_product.

link_bindings.name: customer_to_fm_customer
link_bindings.note: fm-cust-{FM id}.

link_bindings.name: customer_to_sage_and_bc
link_bindings.note: erp_code = Sage IDCUST = BC customer No.; not unique.

link_bindings.name: supplier_to_fm_supplier
link_bindings.note: fm-supp-{n} or the bare FM id, one key under fm_supplier_id (Supplier.same_record_as, verified).

link_bindings.name: project_key
link_bindings.note: Holds the project KEY; mutable in place on DRAFT/SENT/NEGOTIATION quotes.

link_bindings.name: manufacturing_order_to_fm_ao
link_bindings.note: Gold MO is the AO.

link_bindings.name: receipt_to_po_text_join
link_bindings.note: Set by a TRIM(po_number) text match at receipt time.

link_bindings.name: supplier_name
link_bindings.note: Names never anchor an identity.

link_bindings.name: mail_sender_domain
link_bindings.upstream: ontology/mentions.py party_domain (MENTION_FEATURES: a counterparty domain under a distinctive domain of a party the target links to corroborates a stored mention link)
link_bindings.note: A distinctive domain corroborates; it never names the supplier alone.

link_bindings.name: mail_and_sharepoint_mentions
link_bindings.note: A mention found by find_identifiers is a lead to any carrier of its kind; only the identity layer decides.
